To get us started, how do you currently prefer to engage with your athletic training and competition?
Options: [I thrive in individual, self-reliant challenges where success rests entirely on my own discipline and preparation. | I prefer the collaborative energy and tactical complexity of working toward a shared goal within a team unit. | I gravitate toward technical, precision-based disciplines where split-second reaction and fine motor control define the outcome.]
I gravitate toward technical, precision-based disciplines where split-second reaction and fine motor control define the outcome.

When you are in the middle of a high-stakes moment, what kind of competitive environment allows you to reach your peak performance?
Options: [A highly controlled, predictable setting where I can repeat my technical movements perfectly and tune out all external variables. | A fluid, reactive environment where I have to adjust my technique instantly to counter an opponent or changing conditions. | An explosive, high-adrenaline setting where the outcome is decided by a single, perfectly executed burst of energy.]
A highly controlled, predictable setting where I can repeat my technical movements perfectly and tune out all external variables.

Looking toward The Brisbane 2032 Games, how do you see your approach to that perfect, controlled execution evolving as you move from your current training into the intensity of the world's highest competitive stage?
Options: [Focusing on biometric refinement—using advanced data to achieve absolute mechanical perfection. | Focusing on mental fortitude—training to silence the noise so the environment feels perfectly still regardless of the stadium atmosphere. | Focusing on long-term consistency—building a training system so reliable that peak execution becomes second nature under the brightest lights.]
Focusing on mental fortitude—training to silence the noise so the environment feels perfectly still regardless of the stadium atmosphere.

You use your compact stature to generate maximum leverage, carving lines through the snow with a level of control that feels almost instinctive.

In the adaptive pathway for alpine skiing—specifically designed for athletes with lower-limb impairments who compete in a sit-ski—your 55kg build becomes a streamlined instrument of speed. Your precision-based mindset allows you to process the terrain in milliseconds, shifting your weight with surgical accuracy to maintain speed through the tightest turns. You are a force of motion, demonstrating how the same focus you once used to find a target now dictates your path to the podium at high velocity.
